idiom_name: method composed of calls to self._step() helpers
implementation_notes: The Python tutorial states it directly: methods may call other methods through the self argument, so a coordinator whose body only calls self._step() helpers is ordinary Python; the single leading underscore is the PEP 8 convention for non-public, which is what keeps the steps out of the documented API. Module-level functions are the equivalent when a step needs no instance state, and a single expression is better when the whole method is one transformation.
pitfalls: The underscore is a convention only - nothing prevents cart._reserve_stock() from another module, so the boundary is documentation rather than enforcement (name mangling with __step is worse: it breaks subclass access and override detection).
The receiver is explicit: writing reserve_stock() instead of self._reserve_stock() silently calls a module-level function, usually surfacing as an AttributeError or, worse, as a different helper.

Attributes resolve at call time, so instance attributes (including steps) can be replaced at runtime - convenient for tests, dangerous when a monkey-patched step changes what the coordinator does in production.
